how.title: How this is worked out
how.periods: Two periods of the same length: the campaign's window, {{from}} to {{to}} ({{days}} days), and the {{days}} days just before it, {{beforeFrom}} to {{beforeTo}}.

rest.more: Every product no campaign was promoting sold {{before}} units before and {{window}} in the window: the business sold {{percent}}% more anyway.
rest.less: Every product no campaign was promoting sold {{before}} units before and {{window}} in the window: the business sold {{percent}}% less anyway.
rest.same: Every product no campaign was promoting sold {{before}} units before and {{window}} in the window: the business held steady.
rest.none: Nothing else sold in the days before, so there is no business trend to compare with.

how.expected: The promoted products sold {{before}} before. Moving like the rest of the business, they would have sold about {{expected}}.

actual.rise: They actually sold {{window}}. So the campaign is credited with {{extra}} extra units.
actual.none: They actually sold {{window}}: no more than the rest of the business would have given them.

how.earned: They made {{perUnit}} profit a unit in the window: {{extra}} × {{perUnit}} is {{profit}} extra profit.
how.cost: Fees, ad spend, other costs and the products given at cost came to {{cost}}.

verdict.paid: {{profit}} is at least {{cost}}: the campaign paid for itself. Every ৳1 spent brought ৳{{ratio}} of extra profit.
verdict.rose_not_paid: {{profit}} is less than {{cost}}: sales rose, but the campaign did not pay back. Every ৳1 spent brought ৳{{ratio}} of extra profit.
verdict.no_rise: The promoted products did no better than the rest of the business: no rise to credit to the campaign.

hidden.paid: The extra profit covers what the campaign cost: it paid for itself.
hidden.rose_not_paid: Sales rose, but the extra profit did not cover what the campaign cost.
hidden.no_rise: The promoted products did no better than the rest of the business: no rise to credit to the campaign.

how.caveat: What this does not prove: the rise happened during the window, and something else may also have helped, such as a competitor running out of stock. The comparison takes out what lifted the whole business, not what lifted only these products.

sources.title: Which page brings orders that stick
sources.counterOnly: Order sources are the pages and accounts online orders come in through. You sell at the counter only, so there is nothing to compare.
sources.note: Orders placed in the period, whenever they were delivered. Cancelled is out of orders placed, refused out of those not cancelled. Under {{floor}} orders a rate says little, so the count is shown instead. A cancellation by the business (out of stock, a duplicate, cannot deliver) is not held against the page.
sources.empty: No online order came in during this period. Pick a longer period.

types.title: Which kind of promotion paid best
types.note: Only campaigns that could be judged count toward extra profit per ৳1. Cost per first-time customer is the cost of every campaign of that kind, divided by the people who bought for the first time during them.

partners.title: Which partner returned the most
partners.note: Average extra is the extra units across the partner’s judged campaigns. A campaign shared by several partners counts in full for each of them, because its result cannot be split.
partners.empty: No partner worked on a campaign in this period.
